equipment: Wire rack over a sheet pan
method: Pat dry, salt generously on all sides with kosher salt, set uncovered on a rack in the fridge.
Insert the Combustion probe sideways, tip dead center. Set target to 137F.
Steak on rack, into the oven, straight from the fridge. No need to bring it to room temp.
Pull when the probe reads 125F, about 45-60 minutes.
Rest ten minutes while the heaviest pan gets ripping hot.
Thin film of high-smoke-point oil. Sear 60 to 90 seconds per side.
Add a knob of butter, baste for the last 30 seconds.
Remove, dust Bullock's seasoning over both sides. Pepper now.
Rest five minutes. Slice against the grain, serve.
notes: Pull 10-15F below the final target; the sear and rest carry it the rest of the way.
A thick-cut ribeye's fat renders best around 137F.
The probe rules over the clock; times after the oven step are expected, not exact.
salt: Kosher salt, about 1/2 tsp Diamond Crystal per pound (1/4 tsp if Morton or table salt). Flaky finishing salt is too coarse for a two-hour brine.
seasoning: Bullock's Meats Ultimate Steakhouse Prime Rib Steak Seasoning: an additive, not a substitute for the salt. Dust on after the sear only; its cane sugar and dehydrated garlic scorch in the sear pan. Or a pinch in the butter baste.
